subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB393.md landed. SR9's screen now exists as StatementValidation.CheckVariableLengthMove, applied from MoveBinder.BindMoveOf -- the ONE application of the MOVE statement's own rules -- so every implicit move a phrase defines (READ/RETURN ... INTO, WRITE/REWRITE/RELEASE ... FROM) inherits it. The relation itself is the ONE VariableLengthCompatibility module built for the 14.8.2.2 boundary crossing (kb/Work PB204); this is its application to MOVE, never a second copy. A NON-GROUP other operand is refused outright because 8.5.1.12.1 states the prohibition over the other operand ("unless the other operand is a compatible group"), which covers a literal, a figurative constant, a function result, a reference-modified operand (8.4.3.3.4 GR6 makes it elementary) and a level-66 alias (13.18.45). The two negatives pin both halves: the non-group arm and the positional-correspondence arm (8.5.1.12.2, two variable-length groups of equal collapsed length whose dynamic items start at different relative byte positions). conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb393_move_varlen_group is the POSITIVE control that the screen does not reject compatible source. No edition gate is written and none is needed: a variable-length group can only be declared from COBOL-2014. SR9's screen and GR9's transfer landed in ONE change set, as the note required -- screening on top of a run-time abort would only have moved the refusal earlier for programs that still could not execute. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Validation/StatementValidation.cs#CheckVariableLengthMove (kb/Work PB878 deleted StatementValidation.CheckVariableLengthMove; SR9 is MoveTable16.VariableLengthRefusal over MoveTable16.OperandItem (which carries PB907's level-66 THROUGH alias reading), framed as COBOL1931 by MoveBinder.MoveCategoryLegality)
